problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 18{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 18 & -12 & -8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{9}{10}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{20}(13{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(13(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{2}{3}.$
